items.actClause: AN ACT authorizing the leasing of certain parkland for development of a parking facility with roof top park occupying the same parkland footprint such that there is no net parkland loss associated with this facility, and for the construction of associated roadways, a pedestrian foot bridge, a loading dock and other new park amenities, required to support new development of an exhibition hall, cultural space, a wellness center, hotel, restaurants, and a community programming not for profit uniquely located on the Hudson River in a historic former power plant, which site is currently an abandoned brownfield site known as the Glenwood Power Plant, uniquely located on the Hudson River adjacent to John F. Kennedy Marina and Trevor Park in the City of Yonkers, which site lacks any land for parking, and which project was contemplated in the approved May 2009 City of Yonkers Alexander Street Master Plan with a new road network connecting Alexander Street to the south past the Glenwood Power Plant through John F. Kennedy Marina and Trevor Park north to provide increased public access to the Hudson River and enhance said parks through the development of a new sustainable riverfront, transit-oriented project by enhancing the existing parks with new amenities
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S5101

TITLE OF BILL:  An act authorizing the leasing of certain parkland for
development of a parking facility with roof top park occupying the
same parkland footprint such that there is no net parkland loss
associated with this facility, and for the construction of associated
roadways, a pedestrian foot bridge, a loading dock and other new park
amenities, required to support new development of an exhibition hall,
cultural space, a wellness center, hotel, restaurants, and a community
programming not for profit uniquely located on the Hudson River in a
historic former power plant, which site is currently an abandoned
brownfield site known as the Glenwood Power Plant, uniquely located on
the Hudson River adjacent to John F. Kennedy Marina and Trevor Park in
the City of Yonkers, which site lacks any land for parking, and which
project was contemplated in the approved May 2009 City of Yonkers
Alexander Street Master Plan with a new road network connecting
Alexander Street to the south past the Glenwood Power Plant through
John F. Kennedy Marina and Trevor Park north to provide increased
public access to the Hudson River and enhance said parks through the
development of a new sustainable riverfront, transit-oriented project
by enhancing the existing parks with new amenities

PURPOSE:

To authorize the leasing and conveyance of certain parkland for
development of a parking facility with an equivalent size roof top
park, a pedestrian footbridge and roadways required to support a new
development, which is currently and abandoned brownfield site uniquely
located on the Hudson River in a historic former power plant and in
the vicinity of Trevor Park and JFK Marina and Park in the City of
Yonkers.

SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1 sets out legislative findings.

Section 2 (a) authorizes the City of Yonkers to enter into contracts,
leases or rental agreement with Glenwood POH LLC and/or other entities
for a term not to exceed 99 years and to follow for the granting of
easements, licenses, permits and concessions in order to construct the
parking facility, a foot bridge for pedestrian access, ramp into the
new complex, loading dock and associated roadways and other park
amenities.

Section 2 (b) authorizes the alienation of specifically described
parkland for the construction of new facilities and amenities
associated with the development of the abandoned power plant in and in
the vicinity of Trevor Park in the City of Yonkers and to enhance
parkland improvements.

Section 3 stipulates that the authorizations set out in section 2 are
subject to the requirement that the City of Yonkers arrange for the
development of such that the parkland being alienated is not only
replaced in kind but improved from current conditions and additional
property in the City of Yonkers is being dedicated as parkland to
offset the permanent alienation.


Section 4 provides the lease or contract shall include reversion
language should the leased park lands cease to be used for these
authorized purpose.

Section 5 sets immediate effective date.

JUSTIFICATION:

This legislation will facilitate the redevelopment of a currently
abandoned vacant power plant brownfield site on the Hudson River by
allowing for construction of a new parking facility and associated
roadways in the City of Yonkers, which will benefit the development of
an exhibition hall, cultural space, a wellness center, hotel,
restaurants and a community programming non for profit and shall
provide capital improvements directly in the same parks of greater
value than the fair market value of the parkland being alienated
causing said parks to be significantly improved by adding new and
improved parkland amenities larger in size and greater in value that
what is currently present and also dedicated new parkland the
equivalent size of the parkland being alienated.

PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New Bill 2013

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None to the State, undermined to the City of Yonkers.

EFFECTIVE DATE:

Immediately

benefit development of an exhibition hall, cultural space, a wellness
center, hotel and restaurants. The site is located on the Hudson River
in an historic former power plant which is an abandoned brown fields
site known as Glenwood Power Plant located adjacent to the John F.
Kennedy Marina and Trevor Park in the city of Yonkers. The improved
site will benefit the general public by providing enhanced park
recreational use amenities including entertainment, amusement,
education and will improve trade, commerce, tourism, meetings and
other events of a civic, community and general public interest. The
development is declared to be used for public purposes and will
provide better access to the Hudson River waterfront, enhance the use
of the adjacent Glenwood Metro North train, and facilitate the
redevelopment of the abandoned brownfield Glenwood Power Plant site.

for a term not to exceed 99 years and to follow for the granting of
easements, licenses, permits and concessions in order to construct the
parking facility, a foot bridge for pedestrian access, ramp into the


new complex, loading dock and associated roadways and other park
amenities.

Section 2 (b) authorizes the alienation of specifically described
parkland for the construction of new facilities and amenities
associated with the development of the abandoned power plant in and in
the vicinity of Trevor Park in the City of Yonkers and to enhance
parkland improvements.

Section 3 stipulates that the authorizations set out in section 2 are
subject to the requirement that the City of Yonkers arrange for the
development of such that the parkland being alienated is not only
replaced in kind but improved from current conditions and additional
property in the City of Yonkers is being dedicated as parkland to
offset the permanent alienation.

Section 4 provides the lease or contract shall include reversion
language should the leased park lands cease to be used for these
authorized purpose.

Section 5 sets immediate effective date.

JUSTIFICATION:  This legislation will facilitate the redevelopment of
a currently abandoned vacant power plant brownfield site on the Hudson
River by allowing for construction of a new parking facility and
associated roadways in the City of Yonkers, which will benefit the
development of an exhibition hall, cultural space, a wellness center,
hotel, restaurants and a community programming not for profit and
shall provide capital improvements directly in the same parks of
greater value than the fair market value of the parkland being
alienated causing said parks to be significantly improved by adding
new and improved parkland amenities larger in size and greater in
value than what is currently present and also dedicated parkland the
equivalent size of the parkland being alienated.

PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:  New Bill 2013

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:  None to the State, undermined to the City of
